title: kbext.py surface prints the versioned extension API from code, and selfdoc check fails when extending.md's table and the code disagree
goal: kbext.SURFACE is a literal that ast.literal_eval reads and the one registry of the public extension API; it names the points lane, forge, ranker, mcp_tools, ingest_mappers, leak_scan and backlog_commands with their call signatures and the settings keys extensions, extension_paths, backlog, gate_checks, group, leak and locked; each entry is a dict with name, signature and added, with deprecated and removed for a deprecated one; kbext.py surface prints API_VERSION and the registry, --json for tools, exit 0; kb/_self/extending.md holds the same table; selfdoc.extending_problems(text, surface) names each entry missing from either side or different, which selfdoc.py check fails on

clauses.clause: kbext.SURFACE is a literal that ast.literal_eval reads and the one registry of the public extension API

it names the points lane, forge, ranker, mcp_tools, ingest_mappers, leak_scan and backlog_commands with their call signatures and the settings keys extensions, extension_paths, backlog, gate_checks, group, leak and locked
each entry is a dict with name, signature and added, with deprecated and removed for a deprecated one
kbext.py surface prints API_VERSION and the registry, --json for tools, exit 0
selfdoc.extending_problems(text, surface) names each entry missing from either side or different, which selfdoc.py check fails on

notes: Everything not in kbext.SURFACE is internal: extending.md says so in its first lines. The registry names every planned point up front, so the point stories implement a contract that already exists.
